messages:
oncall-bot: Paging SRE: GPU instability detected in inference pool 'r-infer-prod-2'. Multiple containers crashed and nodes flapping. Auto-fallback kicked in for some routes. Please triage. (alert id: INF-RUNTIME-2039-07)

jamie.sre: ack, taking primary. oncall here. Anyone seeing customer-facing errors yet?

alex.infra: seeing repeated driver resets on node gpu-node-17: kernel log shows Xid 13 then 31. nvidia-smi intermittently reports ECC errors.

priya.ops: we've got elevated 5xxs on the hosted API route /v1/generate for a subset of requests ~3% error rate, spike started ~2039123420. Affected customers: two mid-market customers on Dedicated routing + some hosted tenants on r-infer-prod-2.

ethan.runtime: moving logs and metrics now. Early suspicion: thermal/ECC causing GPU soft faults -> driver resets -> container OOM/crash on restart. We're seeing ai-runtime containers CrashLoopBackOff after reset.

jamie.sre: steps: 1) cordon gpu-node-17 2) drain non-critical pods 3) route traffic off node 4) check for pattern across other nodes. I'll cordon now.

# command
jamie.sre: ```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-17
kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

eng-deploy-bot: Canary routing adjustment: shifting 12% of inference traffic from r-infer-prod-2 -> r-infer-prod-1 to reduce tail latency.

alex.infra: posting kernel excerpt: ```
Jul 20 03:42:18 gpu-node-17 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:86:00): 13, PID 2487: Scheduler timeout
Jul 20 03:42:18 gpu-node-17 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:86:00): 31, GPU access fault
Jul 20 03:42:20 gpu-node-17 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:86:00): 18, ECC error corrected
```

priya.ops: customer update drafted: "We're investigating intermittent GPU instability causing higher error rates for some requests. We're routing traffic to alternate capacity and will follow up once nodes are stabilized." Want to post? @cs-helena

cs-helena: please post that and include ETA: we'll follow up in 30m. Also ask customers to escalate via support ticket if they have live incidents.

ethan.runtime: observed containers running out of GPU memory on restart because kv-cache warmup + batching spikes. Stack shows model runner hit OOM then SIGABRT. Sample pod log: ```
[runner] Allocating kv-cache: 3.2GiB
[runner] Batch size 48 -> OOM after commit
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
Aborted (core dumped)
```

jamie.sre: mitigation plan: short-term: drain node, reboot host, disable ECC correction logging (no, we should not disable ECC) — scratch that. Prefer: reprovision node with same image, if flapper persists, mark hardware suspect and move to maintenance. Also enable temporary per-route retry/backoff to reduce batch spikes.

alex.infra: doing a cold-reboot of gpu-node-17 now and pulling dmesg + health checks post boot. If ECC corrected errors persist, hardware ticket with cloud provider.

eng-deploy-bot: Rolling config change: set inference-route /v1/generate retrier: attempts=3, backoff=250ms for affected group. Pushing now.

priya.ops: monitoring dashboards: error-rate dropped from 3.1% -> 1.4% after traffic shift and retrier change. Latency percentiles steady but tail still noisy.

jamie.sre: handoff note for next on-call (copy into PD): cordoned gpu-node-17 due to repeated Xid 13/31/ECC spikes, drained non-essential pods, traffic shifted to r-infer-prod-1, retrier/backoff applied to affected routes, rebooted host (reboot in progress at 2039123560). If node returns healthy, rejoin to cluster with reduced workload and watch for recurrence. If Xid/ECC reappears, escalate to infra for hardware replacement.

alex.infra: reboot finished; dmesg after boot shows immediate ECC corrected count increment and then quiet. nvidia-smi shows all GPUs returned, driver v525.85. Re-joined node as unschedulable (left cordoned). Recommend to keep cordoned for 60m.

ethan.runtime: watching pod restarts. We'll bring a single canary of model-serving pods back on node with reduced batch config (batch=8) to validate. If stable for 10 min, consider soft uncordon for low-priority jobs.

cs-helena: posted update to customers at 2039123695: "Traffic shifted, mitigations applied, monitoring. ETA next update ~30m."

jamie.sre: leaving final action items: 1) alex to file hardware support ticket if ECC/xid recurs 2) ethan to run targeted canary with batch=8 3) priya to monitor customer error queues and update CS 4) next oncall to monitor for 2 hours then close. Adding runbook link: https://runbooks.internal/redwood/gpu-reset-xid (see section 2 for escalation steps).

alex.infra: filing ticket with provider, attaching dmesg and Xid logs. Ticket id prov-342198.

eng-deploy-bot: Incident bot: created incident incident-2039-07 (severity: P2), assigned to SRE.

jamie.sre: handing off to night oncall in 10m. Final note: no evidence of software regression; pattern looks hardware/driver. If anyone sees broad model failures beyond this pool, ping me and escalate to ENG runtime.

priya.ops: last check at 2039123830: error-rate 0.9% and falling. marking as monitoring and will update PD in 30m unless regression. :white_check_mark:
